false_assumption.statement: Captain Marchal, the blind secretary, was the murderer motivated by unrequited love.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The physiological test showed Captain Marchal's emotional reactions to the reconstructed murder scene, and his delirious mutterings suggested knowledge of the crime. His close presence at the crime scene and his nervous behavior made him a plausible suspect.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It obscures the real culprit's identity and the fact that Marchal was a victim who had discovered the truth and was silenced before he could expose the murderer.

mechanism_description: Leonidas Hoyos, under the alias Eric Vivaseur, killed Evelyn Jarvis to prevent exposure of their past and to recover letters that blackmailed her. He broke into the Norwood museum using a spider tool to pick the lock, confronted Evelyn who came to retrieve the letters, and strangled her. Later, he murdered Victor Marchal who had discovered the truth and staged his death as a suicide by firing two shots, one blank, to mislead investigators.

discriminating_test.design: McCarty gathers all key persons in his rooms and recounts the full story of the past and present crimes, revealing the connections and evidence. The presence and reactions of the accused, Eric Vivaseur, are observed to confirm his guilt. The test uses the signed statement of Victor Marchal and the recovered evidence to confront the culprit.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals the true identity of the murderer and his motive, exposing the deception and clearing innocent suspects.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The culprit's presence and inability to refute the evidence confirms his guilt without relying on confessions or behavioral cues.
